About Me

I completed my BSc (Honors) in Physics at Jagannath University in 2025, ranking second in my department, and I am now completing my MSc there, with expected completion in early 2027.

My research follows materials from synthesis to measurement. I prepare ferrites and ceramics by auto-combustion and solid-state reaction, characterize their structure and morphology, and study how composition controls their magnetic and dielectric behavior. I have also simulated metamaterial resonators in CST Microwave Studio and contributed to the green synthesis of nanomaterials.

My goal is to build a research career in materials science through doctoral study and international research training, starting with a PhD in 2027.

Research

Spinel ferrites and perovskite ceramics are the core of my work, alongside green nanomaterial synthesis and electromagnetic simulation.

MSc thesis, ongoing

Tuning Magnetic and Dielectric Properties of Mn-Substituted Ni–Zn–Co–Al Nanoferrites

Supervisor: Dr. Abdullah Al Momin, Jagannath University

I am studying how Mn substitution governs structure–property relationships in Ni–Zn–Co–Al nanoferrites prepared by auto-combustion. The target applications are MHz inductors and EMI-suppression cores, where magnetic and dielectric behavior have to be balanced.

Status, October 2026: samples are synthesized, shaped and sintered at three temperatures; density measurements are under way to choose the optimum. Next: XRD, FESEM, EDX and FTIR, then VSM and impedance analysis, to relate cation distribution to saturation magnetization, coercivity, dielectric constant and AC conductivity.

  • Auto-combustion
  • XRD
  • FESEM
  • EDX
  • FTIR
  • VSM
  • Impedance

Spinel ferrites, poster at BCA 2025

Nickel-Tuned Functional Properties in Mn–Zn–Cu–Al Ferrites

Dr. Abdullah Al Momin’s group, Jagannath University

Mn0.5−xNixZn0.4Cu0.1Fe1.95Al0.05O4 (x = 0–0.40), prepared by auto-combustion, calcined at 700 °C and sintered at 1100 °C, for high-frequency multilayer chip inductors.

  • Single-phase cubic spinel; the lattice constant falls with Ni content, following Vegard’s law
  • Higher density and larger grains, from 1.61 to 2.55 µm
  • Initial permeability up more than 3.5 times and relative quality factor more than 6 times, compared with the parent composition
  • Conduction by small-polaron hopping, with grain boundaries dominating the resistance
  • Auto-combustion
  • XRD
  • FESEM
  • Initial permeability
  • Impedance analysis

Perovskite ceramics, poster at ICEI 2026

Lead-Free Zr-Doped Ba–Li–Gd–Sr–Ti Perovskite Ceramics

Dr. Abdullah Al Momin’s group, Jagannath University

Ba0.5Li0.1Gd0.1Sr0.3ZrxTi1−xO3 (BLGSZT, x = 0–0.10), prepared by solid-state reaction as a lead-free magnetodielectric material.

  • Single-phase distorted tetragonal perovskite
  • Zr increases the average grain size from 1.34 to 1.83 µm
  • Relative quality factor rises from about 42 to 72, while the dielectric constant decreases
  • AC conduction by small-polaron hopping, suppressed by Zr substitution

My part: XRD, FESEM and EDX characterization and co-analysis of the results, under the guidance of a senior thesis student.

  • Solid-state reaction
  • XRD
  • FESEM
  • EDX
  • Impedance analysis
